value: One of only three grapes allowed in the DO, made into traditional method sparkling wine, usually blended with Pinot Noir.
source_notes: INPI DO specification: only Chardonnay, Pinot Noir and Riesling Itálico authorised; traditional method only, Charmat not allowed. SevenFifty Daily: DO exclusively for traditional method sparkling; wines generally a mix of Pinot Noir and Chardonnay.

value: One of only three grapes allowed in the DO, made into traditional method sparkling wine, usually blended with Chardonnay.
source_notes: INPI DO specification: only Chardonnay, Pinot Noir and Riesling Itálico authorised; traditional method only. SevenFifty Daily: wines generally a mix of Pinot Noir and Chardonnay.

value: Authorised for wines of the Campanha Gaúcha indication of provenance, and made there as a varietal red, in blends and in rosé.
source_notes: Embrapa IP chapter: Cabernet Sauvignon authorised; varietal and blended reds; rosés mainly from Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot and Pinot Noir. WineTourism.com Brazil guide lists Cabernet Sauvignon among Campanha reds (lower tier).

value: Authorised for wines of the Campanha Gaúcha indication of provenance, and made there as a varietal white and as the main grape of its sparkling wines.
source_notes: Embrapa IP chapter: Chardonnay authorised; most whites are varietals of Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc and others; sparkling wines use above all Chardonnay or Chardonnay blends. WineTourism.com Brazil guide lists Chardonnay among Campanha whites (lower tier).

value: Authorised for wines of the Campanha Gaúcha indication of provenance, and made there as a varietal red, in blends and in rosé.
source_notes: Embrapa IP chapter: Merlot authorised; varietal and blended reds; rosés mainly from Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot and Pinot Noir. WineTourism.com Brazil guide lists Merlot among Campanha reds (lower tier).

value: Authorised for wines of the Campanha Gaúcha indication of provenance, and made there as a red, as a rosé and in sparkling blends with Chardonnay.
source_notes: Embrapa IP chapter: Pinot Noir authorised; varietal reds, rosés, and sparkling of Chardonnay blended with Pinot Noir among others. WineTourism.com Brazil guide lists Pinot Noir among Campanha reds (lower tier).

value: Authorised for wines of the Campanha Gaúcha indication of provenance, and made there both as a varietal red and in blends.
source_notes: Embrapa chapter reproducing the IP Campanha Gaúcha specification: Tannat on the authorised list; reds are varietals of Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon, Tannat, Cabernet Franc, Pinot Noir and others, or blends. SevenFifty Daily: Tannat largely found in Serra do Sudeste and Campanha Gaúcha.

value: The region's signature red grape, typically made into structured red wines that can age.
source_notes: Decanter (sponsor content created with Uruguay Wine): Tannat became the champion of the region; the more structured, ageworthy Tannat so typical of the region. SevenFifty Daily (Amanda Barnes): although Tannat dominates, a wide range of grapes are planted in Canelones.

value: Close to the Atlantic it makes tangy, savoury whites with a clear maritime character.
source_notes: World of Fine Wine (Amanda Barnes): punchy yet refined Albariño from Maldonado, tangy maritime whites. Wine Folly: Maldonado produces saline and savory examples of Albariño.

value: Here the ocean and granite soils give Tannat more freshness and a mineral energy.
source_notes: Decanter (sponsor content with Uruguay Wine): coastal influence and granite, rocky soils give Tannat wines with more freshness and brightness. World of Fine Wine: the mineral verve of the Tannat; climate gives a lot of energy to the wines. Wine Folly: mineral rich, powerful wines, especially Tannat.

value: One of Niagara's main grapes, at its most distinctive on the limestone bench sites below the escarpment.
source_notes: World of Fine Wine: Bench terroir most eloquently expressed by Chardonnay and Pinot Noir, reflecting the limestone; VQA Ontario Twenty Mile Bench page: supports classic cool climate varieties, notably Pinot Noir, Chardonnay, Riesling; VQA Niagara Peninsula page: Chardonnay among classic varieties that flourish

value: One of Niagara's classic cool climate grapes, at its most distinctive on the limestone bench sites below the escarpment.
source_notes: World of Fine Wine: Bench terroir most eloquently expressed by Chardonnay and Pinot Noir; St David's Bench not well suited; VQA Ontario Twenty Mile Bench page: notably Pinot Noir; VQA Niagara Peninsula page: Pinot Noir among classic cool climate varieties

value: Made dry, off dry and sweet, and with Vidal one of the two main grapes for Icewine.
source_notes: World of Fine Wine: dry and off dry Niagara Rieslings; Wine Country Ontario Icewine page (403, search snippet only): majority of Icewine made from Riesling and Vidal (Ontario wide); Wine Folly: popular ice wine varieties include Riesling and Vidal (not Canada specific)

value: Acidity runs high in Niagara Riesling, so many are made off dry to balance it, though more dry versions are now made.
source_notes: World of Fine Wine: acidity is high and the market wanted residual sugar to balance it; dry versions rising; VQA Ontario one pager: crisp acidity, residual sugar adjusted to style; Decanter (search snippet only, paywalled): producers mastered off dry, dry styles once atypical

value: Grown for traditional method sparkling wine, often blended with Pinot Noir, as well as for still wines, and allowed as a minor partner in a Tidal Bay blend.
source_notes: Wines of Nova Scotia article: Tidal Bay at least 51% L'Acadie/Seyval/Vidal/Geisenheim 318-57, up to 49% others incl. Chardonnay; varietal still Chardonnays (Blomidon); sparkling the hero; Wine Anorak: Benjamin Bridge traditional method blends of Chardonnay and Pinot Noir (single producer)

value: In Nova Scotia it gives crisp whites with citrus notes and enough body to be aged in barrel.
source_notes: Taste of Nova Scotia: crisp acidity, notes of citrus and grass, often barrel aged; Bishop's Cellar (Halifax retailer): crisp apple and citrus, richer and fuller bodied than Seyval Blanc, barrel influenced styles

value: Grown in the warm south of the valley, where many of the best reds are Bordeaux style blends that include it.
source_notes: Wine Anorak (Jamie Goode): Cabernet Franc and Sauvignon excel in the south, where many of the best wines are Bordeaux blends; GuildSomm (Rhys Pender MW): Syrah, Merlot and the Cabernets succeed in the south; Wine Folly: a Bordeaux blend grape on the eastern benches

value: Here it tastes riper and rounder than in the Loire, with cocoa and dried pepper notes over juicy fruit and moderate, smooth tannins.
source_notes: Wine Folly (Okanagan): dried pepper flakes, cherry sauce, cocoa, riper and sweeter than Loire, suede like tannins; GuildSomm (BC wide, not Okanagan specific): juicy, fresh, moderate tannins, typically riper than the Loire

value: Grown in the warmest southern sites, where it can still struggle to ripen in some years, and it often goes into Bordeaux style blends.
source_notes: GuildSomm: the Cabernets succeed in the south; can struggle to ripen in some vintages; Wine Folly: seems to have trouble here; Wine Anorak: excels in the south (Osoyoos) where many of the best wines are Bordeaux blends

value: Grown throughout the valley, from the warm south to the cooler north around Kelowna.
source_notes: Wine Anorak: Chardonnay does well throughout the valley; Wine Folly: best southern vines on the west side, and in the north in East Kelowna

value: Grown in the south and centre of the valley, and a main part of the region's Bordeaux style red blends.
source_notes: GuildSomm: Merlot among successful varieties in the south and in the middle of the valley; Wine Folly: main component of the Bordeaux style blends that are the focus; Wine Anorak: widely planted, backbone of many commercial wines

value: Leaner and firmer than most Merlot, with notable tannin and lively natural acidity.
source_notes: GuildSomm (BC wide): very structured with natural high tannin and acidity, more tannic than Californian or Bordeaux examples; Wine Folly (Okanagan): like Bordeaux but leaner and fruitier

value: A mainstay white of the valley, grown especially in the cooler north.
source_notes: Wine Anorak: among the most widely planted, commercial backbone, suited to the cool north (Lake Country); GuildSomm: Pinot Gris in the cooler northern parts; Wine Folly: a standby in the Okanagan

value: Here it is crisp and fresh with high acidity and a lean finish, only turning richer when aged in oak.
source_notes: Wine Folly (Okanagan): sky high acidity, lean tingly finish; GuildSomm (BC wide): typically crisp and fresh, oak aged versions richer and fuller

value: Grown mainly in the cooler north of the valley, around Kelowna and Lake Country.
source_notes: GuildSomm: Pinot Noir in the cooler northern parts and the middle of the valley; Wine Anorak: cooler areas, mainly the north, doing really well; Wine Folly: East Kelowna in the north

value: It tends to be fresh and high in acid with firmer tannins than many Pinot Noirs, so it is rarely as light as Burgundy.
source_notes: GuildSomm (BC wide): fresh acidity, solid tannins, not generally as light as Burgundy; Wine Folly (Okanagan): high acidity, crunchy tannins

value: A lead grape of the County, made both as still wine and as traditional method sparkling.
source_notes: WineAlign special report: Chardonnay the most consistent grape and calling card of the County, suited to still and traditional method sparkling; Wine Anorak: hot spot for Chardonnay, Pinot Noir and sparkling; VQA Ontario: Chardonnay listed first among common varieties

value: Taut and fresh, it ripens at modest alcohol with high acidity in the cool County climate.
source_notes: World of Fine Wine: County Chardonnay shows charismatic tension; WineAlign: County reaches ripe flavours at low potential alcohol and high acidity; Wine Anorak: 12% alcohol is normal, some fully ripe at 10.5%

value: Grown alongside Chardonnay as one of the County's two lead grapes, planted for its limestone soils and cool climate.
source_notes: Wine Anorak: Heinricks saw potential for world class Pinot Noir and Chardonnay given limestone soils and Burgundy like degree days; WineAlign: Pinot Noir truly excellent at its best but harder to grow; VQA Ontario: listed among common varieties

value: Pale, light bodied and crisp, it ripens at modest alcohol and often shows a saline, mineral finish.
source_notes: WineAlign: pale, transparent, fragrant, as savoury as fruity; World of Fine Wine: light bodied, swift and crisp with plenty of salinity, ripe at about 12%; VQA Ontario: elegant cool climate Pinots with pronounced minerality on the finish

value: One of the main white grapes here, made as a still white wine.
source_notes: Querétaro state tourism board lists chardonnay among the main white grapes; Mexico News Daily: table wines are made from chardonnay among other international grapes; International Wine Challenge listing (search result, wid 185007): Freixenet Sala Vivé Brut Rosé from Querétaro made from Pinot Noir and Chardonnay (style: sparkling). Sparkling use rests on one competition listing plus the producer. [Lead agent: sparkling use dropped from value, it rested on one competition listing.]

value: One of the main red grapes here, made as a still red wine.
source_notes: Querétaro state tourism board: main red grapes are Merlot, Syrah, Malbec, Marselan, Tempranillo and Cabernet; Mexico News Daily: table wines made from merlot, syrah, chardonnay and sauvignon blanc.

value: One of the main white grapes here, made as a still white wine.
source_notes: Querétaro state tourism board lists sauvignon blanc among the main white grapes; Mexico News Daily: table wines made from merlot, syrah, chardonnay and sauvignon blanc.

value: One of the main red grapes here, made as a still red wine.
source_notes: Querétaro state tourism board lists Syrah (spelled Syrha) among the main red grapes; Mexico News Daily: table wines made from merlot, syrah, chardonnay and sauvignon blanc.

value: One of the main grapes of Sussex traditional method sparkling wine, and the grape of its Blanc de Blancs, which must be at least 90 percent Chardonnay. It is also allowed for still wine.
source_notes: Sussex PDO specification (DEFRA): Chardonnay permitted for sparkling and still; Blanc de Blancs at least 90% Chardonnay. Wine Folly: Chardonnay, Pinot Noir and Pinot Meunier are the 3 primary grapes of English traditional method sparkling; Sussex chalk suits sparkling.

value: In Sussex it gives taut, high acid sparkling wine, often described as chalky and mineral, with toast and brioche notes from long ageing on the lees.
source_notes: Sussex PDO specification: crisp acidity from the chardonnays; long on lees ageing gives brioche, fresh toast and honey; chalk imparts a distinctive character. Wine Folly: cool climate preserves acidity; Sussex wines often described as chalky, flint, strong mineral character (region wide, not Chardonnay specific).

value: One of the main grapes of Sussex traditional method sparkling wine, where it can join Pinot Noir in a Blanc de Noirs. It is also allowed for still wine.
source_notes: Sussex PDO specification lists Pinot Meunier for sparkling and still wine; Blanc de Noirs at least 90% Pinot Noir and/or Pinot Meunier. Wine Folly: Pinot Meunier one of the 3 primary grapes of English traditional method sparkling.

value: One of the main grapes of Sussex traditional method sparkling wine, alone or with Pinot Meunier in a Blanc de Noirs, which must be at least 90 percent of these two grapes. It is also allowed for still wine.
source_notes: Sussex PDO specification: Pinot Noir permitted for sparkling and still; Blanc de Noirs at least 90% Pinot Noir and/or Pinot Meunier. Wine Folly: one of the 3 primary grapes of English traditional method sparkling.

value: Authorised for the red wines of the Vale do São Francisco indication of provenance, and with Tempranillo the main red grape grown there.
source_notes: INPI IP Vale do São Francisco specification: Syrah on the authorised red list. Bragantia (peer reviewed journal, SciELO): Syrah and Tempranillo are the principal cultivars for red wine in this semiarid region.

value: Authorised for the red wines of the Vale do São Francisco indication of provenance, and with Syrah the main red grape grown there.
source_notes: INPI IP Vale do São Francisco specification: Tempranillo on the authorised red list. Bragantia (peer reviewed journal, SciELO): Syrah and Tempranillo are the principal cultivars for red wine in this semiarid region.

value: A complementary grape allowed in DO red blends, which Merlot must lead.
source_notes: Embrapa (DO Vale dos Vinhedos viticultural register, ch. I): Merlot and Chardonnay are the DO grapes; Cabernet Sauvignon, Cabernet Franc and Tannat complementary; reds at least 60% Merlot. WineTourism.com: Merlot the key red; Cabernet Sauvignon, Cabernet Franc and Tannat also permitted in blends (lower tier).

value: A complementary grape allowed in DO red blends, which Merlot must lead.
source_notes: Embrapa (DO Vale dos Vinhedos register, ch. I): Tannat a complementary red; reds at least 60% Merlot. WineTourism.com: Cabernet Sauvignon, Cabernet Franc and Tannat also permitted in blends (lower tier).

value: Bottled here as a varietal red, though much of the vine grown under this name is thought to be a mix of other varieties rather than true Nebbiolo alone.
source_notes: Lodi Winegrape Commission blog quotes Wine Enthusiast (Nils Bernstein): Baja produces a lot of wine labeled Nebbiolo, some tested grapes came back as Lambrusca di Alessandria; Anaya family told Valle de Guadalupe Nebbiolo is not truly Nebbiolo. Exotic Wine Travel: Mexican Nebbiolo is probably not a single variety but several. Identity of the vine is disputed.

value: Wine sold as Nebbiolo here is darker, riper and fuller bodied than in Piedmont, with ripe black fruit.
source_notes: Exotic Wine Travel: Mexican Nebbiolo makes darker, less tannic wine than Italian, riper darker fruit, bigger plusher body. Lodi Winegrape Commission: deep colored, rich Nebbiolo of Valle de Guadalupe; quotes Wine Enthusiast: inky wines with jammy black fruit, no resemblance to Italian versions.
